2026-12-09.title: Wednesday of the Second Week of Advent
readings: The Lord gives strength to the weary
O bless the Lord, my soul!
Come to me, all you that are weary
2026-12-09.alt: Optional memorial: St Juan Diego Cuauhtlatoatzin.
2026-12-09.verse: Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest.
theo: Isaiah speaks to exiles who think God has forgotten them: “My way is hidden from the LORD.” The prophet answers: the Creator of the stars, who calls each by name, “does not faint or grow weary… He gives power to the faint… those who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength, they shall mount up with wings like eagles.” Waiting on God is not passive; it is where strength comes from.

Jesus speaks the same promise in person: “Come to me, all you that are weary… I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me; for I am gentle and humble in heart.” A yoke joins two animals to share a load; Jesus offers to carry our burden with us. St Juan Diego, a humble Mexican Indian, was the one Our Lady sent to the bishop in 1531; God chose the weary and little to carry his message.
outline: Ask: what burden are you carrying alone right now?
The Creator gives strength to the faint.
“My yoke is easy, and my burden is light.”
live: Spend ten minutes before the Blessed Sacrament and hand over one burden.
Help someone who is overloaded this week.
2026-12-09.prayer: Lord Jesus, gentle and humble of heart, I come to you tired and burdened. Take my yoke with me, renew my strength, and teach me to wait on you and rise on eagles' wings. Amen.
altar: At Mass Jesus says again: come to me. In Holy Communion he gives rest to the weary and strength to the faint.

quick: Jesus invites the weary to rest in him.
Those who wait on the Lord renew their strength.
2026-12-09.action: Hand over one burden to Jesus before the tabernacle.
2026-12-09.question: What burden am I carrying without Jesus?

family.explain: Jesus says: come to me when you are tired, and I will give you rest. He is gentle and kind.
family.intention: We pray for parents, grandparents and all who are tired.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we help someone in our family who is tired this week?”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, gentle and humble of heart, you call the weary to yourself. As we gather, we bring you our burdens; give us your rest. Amen.
share: Isaiah says God calls the stars by name (Isaiah 40:26). How does it feel to know God knows me by name?
Jesus says: come to me, all who are weary (Matthew 11:28). What is my heaviest burden?
How can I make time to rest in the Lord this Advent?
interc: For the Church, that she may be a place of rest for the weary.
For parents and caregivers who are exhausted.
For workers abroad and those in hard labour.
For the sick and the elderly, that they may renew their strength in the Lord.
For our group, that we may help carry one another's burdens.
pm.close: Lord God, you give power to the faint. Renew our strength, teach us to rest in your Son, and let us learn from his gentle and humble heart. Amen.

illus: A nurse working night shifts in a Delhi hospital said: “On my way home every morning I stop for ten minutes at the chapel. I don't say much. I just give him the night. I leave lighter than I came.”

homily: Dear friends, Isaiah asks: to whom then will you compare me? Lift up your eyes on high and see: who created these? He who brings out their host and numbers them, calling them all by name (Isaiah 40:25–26). The God of countless stars knows each one by name. He knows you by name too.

Then Isaiah answers the complaint of a tired people: why do you say, my way is hidden from the Lord? The Lord is the everlasting God. He does not faint or grow weary. He gives power to the faint. Those who wait for the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles; they shall run and not be weary, they shall walk and not faint (Isaiah 40:27–31).

In the Gospel Jesus says one of his most loved invitations: come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me; for I am gentle and humble in heart (Matthew 11:28–29).

Many of us are tired: parents juggling work and children, students under pressure, workers abroad, the sick, the old, the caregivers. December can make us even more tired with its rush. Jesus does not say: try harder. He says: come to me.
A yoke is a wooden frame that joins two oxen so that they pull together. Jesus offers to share our yoke. We do not carry life alone. His yoke is easy because he carries most of the weight.

This Advent, let us find a little time each day simply to rest in the Lord: a quiet moment in a church, a visit to the Blessed Sacrament, five minutes of silence. Those who wait for the Lord shall renew their strength. Amen.
kids: Children, when you are tired or sad, Jesus says: come to me. You can always tell Him how you feel!

intro: God never grows weary; Jesus gives rest; waiting on the Lord renews strength.

sub: He gives power to the faint.
q: Have you not known? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He does not faint or grow weary; his understanding is unsearchable. He gives power to the faint, and strengthens the powerless.
Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest.
points.apply: Tell God honestly where you are tired.

sub: His burden is light because he carries it with us.
q: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and do not forget all his benefits—who forgives all your iniquity, who heals all your diseases.
Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me; for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
points.apply: Help carry someone else's load this week.

sub: Waiting on God is active trust.
God chose the humble Juan Diego.
He reveals himself to the little ones.
q: But those who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength, they shall mount up with wings like eagles, they shall run and not be weary, they shall walk and not faint.

At that same hour Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, “I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and the intelligent and have revealed them to infants.”
points.apply: Spend ten minutes in silent prayer today.

concl: The weary find rest in Christ.
Wait on the Lord, and rise.
2026-12-09.resolve: Visit the Blessed Sacrament once this week.
